hypothesis: The published ShuffleNetV2 graph runs on the interrupt-driven finite image at 492 and 852 MHz and its job time follows T(f) = C/f + M.
prediction:
The NPU's feature record gives 8 NN cores, 512 KiB of VIP SRAM and a 16-byte AXI bus (vip2/inc/vip_feature_database.h:161-183). Decoding the 125 NN descriptors with the field layout of the Mesa etnaviv driver (etnaviv_ml_nn.c:31-140) gives about 0.59 G multiply-accumulates, four times ShuffleNetV2's nominal 146 M because the compiled graph runs the first convolution at 224 x 224 before subsampling and the last 1 x 1 convolution at 14 x 14; an estimate of the engine's work, not a measurement. A job's time at NPU clock f is T(f) = C/f + M, with C cycles of clock-bound work and M of clock-independent memory and latency time; the one-operation convolution measured C about 0 and M about 4.3 us.
| Quantity | Central prediction | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C, at about 590 effective MACs per cycle | 1.0 M cycles | 0.4–2.5 M |
| M, DRAM traffic of 0.9 MB of coefficients and the pool, and per-operation latency | 0.8 ms | 0.3–2 ms |
| Doorbell to interrupt, 492 MHz | 2.8 ms | 1.5–6 ms |
| Doorbell to interrupt, 852 MHz | 2.0 ms | 1.0–5 ms |
| Time ratio 852/492 | 0.72 | 0.6–0.9; 0.58 if wholly clock bound |
| Active-cycle ratio 852/492, (C + M·852 MHz)/(C + M·492 MHz) | 1.21 | 1.0–1.5 |
| Idle share of the job's cycles | under 10% | the convolution: 90% |
The two starts determine C and M: C = (T492 - T852)/(1/492 MHz - 1/852 MHz) and M = T492 - C/492 MHz, which the set's timing.py --compare computes. Both outputs match the reference [0,255] at both rates and startup stays at 4.0 ms. Submit and publish phases run on the CPU before the doorbell and were predicted at 1-5 ms and 5-30 ms per job, dominated by clearing the pool and hashing about 0.92 MB with the software SHA-256.
conclusion: Measured (set 16, port 3-3): doorbell to interrupt 2.91 ms at 852 MHz and 3.69 ms at 492 MHz, giving C about 902,000 NPU cycles and M about 1.85 ms, above the predicted central M of 0.8 ms; ratio 852/492 = 0.79, inside the predicted 0.6-0.9 range. The publication phase measured 55.8-56.1 ms per job (CPU hashing and translation), above the predicted 5-30 ms; see docs/evidence/npu-job-overhead.jsonl. The 2-byte output [0,255] is saturated, so a match is weak evidence of correct arithmetic: no unsaturated intermediate or larger reference exists for this graph. A later run could compare an unsaturated layer output with the SDK's vpm_run --layer_dump (examples/vpm_run/vpm_run.c:57, :2411-2428), read from the DRAM pool before the host restores DRAM.
narrative: Image: apps/npu-finite/build.py --interrupt --shufflenet at 492 MHz and --rate-852 at 852 MHz, one cold lifetime on port 3-3, runbook docs/board-runbooks/npu-full-model.md. Per-layer times need a completion per operation; the compiled command raises one event after all 125 operations, so the run times the whole graph. Host files byte-identical to the reviewed interrupt host (board-bundles-20261025-13); host fixtures also cover a reference shorter than 100 bytes.

hypothesis: The fixed 23 us from publication to interrupt of a one-operation job is dominated by NPU register accesses at about 1.6 us each, plus about 4.3 us of memory-latency-bound NPU work.
prediction: Proposed reductions (all since implemented, see docs/designs/npu-job-overhead.md): plain register access predicted to bring an access to 0.1-0.3 us (publication to doorbell 11 -> about 2 us; publication to interrupt 23 -> about 14 us; interrupt to completion 16 -> about 8 us); the two-write trigger removes five reads (with plain access publication to doorbell about 1 us, publication to interrupt about 13 us; alone about 8 us); one event read at completion (with plain access interrupt to completion about 6 us); immutable buffers prepared once remove the publish phase's hash and most of its 19,442 cache lines.
conclusion:
- **Cost of one register access.** The start timestamp follows the
  total-cycle read by the rest of that read and the whole idle-cycle read;
  the completion timestamp precedes the total-cycle read by one adapter-clock
  read, the whole idle-cycle read and the total-cycle read up to its sample.
  The window difference, 5.0 µs on average, therefore spans three register
  reads and one clock read: about 1.6 µs per NPU register access.
- **Publication to doorbell, about 11 µs, estimated.** After the start
  timestamp the controller reads three configuration registers, the idle
  register and the event register, writes `+0x654` and `+0x3A4`, and issues
  two `DSB SY` barriers (`a733_npu_controller.c:78-93`): seven accesses,
  7 × 1.6 µs.
- **NPU work, 4.0–4.4 µs.** The active cycles are 2,000–2,200 at 492 MHz and
  3,400–3,700 at 852 MHz, the same 4.3 µs at both clocks, so memory latency
  bounds it: command fetch, descriptor, kernel and input reads and the output
  write, all from DRAM.
- **About 8 µs not yet attributed**: 23.3 − 11 − 4.3 µs. It holds interrupt
  delivery and exception entry and any NPU time between the doorbell and the
  first active cycle or after the last one that the counters record as idle.
- **Interrupt to completion record, 16 µs.** The worker reads three
  configuration registers, the event register, the idle register and the
  event register again (`a733_npu_controller.c:211-228`): 6 × 1.6 µs, about
  10 µs, and about 6 µs of wake, GIC mask and clock reads.

Each access includes the bus access to the NPU's registers, a translation of
the register address with `AT` and a `PAR_EL1` decode
(`platform/a733/npu_native.c:94-113`, `include/a733_mapping_check.h:62-77`),
and `DSB SY` around it (`include/a733_mmio.h:54-64`). These records do not
separate the bus latency from the translation and barrier cost. The doorbell
timestamp of the ShuffleNetV2 run measures publication to doorbell directly,
and with it doorbell to interrupt, which bounds the unattributed 8 µs.
narrative:
Set 13 (board-session-20261025-9/port-3-3) timed four one-operation jobs.

| Job | Total-cycle window | System-counter window | Difference | Active | Publication to interrupt | Interrupt to completion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 492 MHz, 1 | 45.35 µs | 40.08 µs | 5.27 µs | 4.37 µs | 23.54 µs | 16.54 µs |
| 492 MHz, 2 | 43.30 µs | 38.54 µs | 4.76 µs | 4.10 µs | 22.71 µs | 15.83 µs |
| 852 MHz, 1 | 44.88 µs | 39.50 µs | 5.38 µs | 4.38 µs | 23.88 µs | 15.62 µs |
| 852 MHz, 2 | 43.56 µs | 38.83 µs | 4.73 µs | 4.00 µs | 23.04 µs | 15.79 µs |

Each register access includes the bus access, a translation of the register address with AT and a PAR_EL1 decode (platform/a733/npu_native.c:94-113, include/a733_mapping_check.h:62-77) and DSB SY around it (include/a733_mmio.h:54-64); the records do not separate bus latency from translation and barrier cost. Per-job phases: Submit (clear the 1,093,632-byte pool, copy the 150,528-byte input, queue hand-off), Publish (hash coefficients, descriptors and job command; clean and invalidate 19,442 cache lines), Pre-trigger (seven NPU register accesses), NPU (doorbell to interrupt), Completion (worker wake and six NPU register reads). The memory-latency part of the one-operation job, 4.3 us, does not change with the NPU clock and none of the reductions addresses it.

hypothesis: The job-phase timestamps change code only in the images that link the convolution backend.
conclusion: Against bringup c4eadf9f, 21 of 68 default images change. The NPU images that link the convolution backend change in code (accelerator composition, convolution model, the four finite profiles); the others differ only in build identity and debug information. The retained large-graph image keeps its layout: USB staging at 0x41400000..0x414c0000, the pool at 0x41600000..0x41a00000 and an equal text size; it gains the __npu_graph_staging symbol and the timestamps. Checks: ~/.cache/sunstoneos/evidence/npu-full-model-1025/full-model-checks.sh builds the ShuffleNetV2 image at 492 and 852 MHz and runs the finite return, SRAM routing, adapter, quiescence, interrupt client, interrupt routing, task profile, reference-clock and interrupt host checks; the convolution model checks the order of the new timestamps and the interrupt client check checks the logged NPU_JOB_PHASES block.
